rubriker.title: Samarkand R2 (women): Georgia only manage a draw against Montenegro
rubriker._rss_content: Georgia became the first leading team to drop match points in the Women's Chess Olympiad, as the second seeds were held to a 2–2 draw by Montenegro in round two. Alena Skvortsova and Aleksandra Milovic (pictured) scored the Montenegrins' two wins. The Czech Republic were also held by the United Arab Emirates, while Tajikistan and Kenya recorded notable match victories against higher-seeded opposition. | Photo: Michal Walusza / FIDE

rubriker.title: Samarkand R2 (open): Despite close calls, all top teams grab wins
rubriker._rss_content: All of the top 28 seeds won in round two of the open Chess Olympiad, but several favourites were pushed hard. The United States (pictured), India and the Netherlands all prevailed by 2½–1½, while El Salvador produced the biggest team upset by beating Cuba. Gukesh Dommaraju was held to a draw by Satria Duta Cahaia and slipped below 2700 on the live rating list. | Photo: Rafal Oleksiewicz / FIDE

rubriker.title: Poland crowned champions at Olympiad for People with Disabilities
rubriker._rss_content: Poland won the 3rd FIDE Chess Olympiad for People with Disabilities in Samarkand after finishing unbeaten on 13 match points, ahead of Cuba and hosts Uzbekistan 1. The final round saw Poland defeat the Philippines 3½–½ to secure gold. The event featured a record 41 teams and was staged alongside the main FIDE Chess Olympiad for the first time. | Photos: Mark Livshitz and Rafal Oleksiewicz

rubriker.title: On the Superfluity of Words (2)
rubriker._rss_content: In today's article we present a gem of chess composition. It is a study requires no words, no instruction or stipulation, such as, for example, "White to move and win". Everything is solved by simply analysing the diagram. Can you follow the logic that tells you everything abut this diagram? It is extensive, exacting, and truly dizzying.
